evidence: Clear module-based grouping (plugins/, helper_funcs/, database/) suggests separation of concerns without full decoupling
Shared dependencies across modules (e.g., plugins importing from helper_funcs, database, translation)
No explicit service boundaries or inter-process communication (e.g., no gRPC, REST clients, message queues)
Single entry point (bot.py) and shared configuration (Config in sample_config.py)
Database layer tightly coupled with business logic (SQLAlchemy ORM classes and sessions in database/)
High average fan-out (6.2) indicates modules depend on many others, typical of tightly coupled monoliths
risks: High coupling between modules (e.g., plugins directly importing and using database tables) reduces testability and maintainability
No isolation between concerns — business logic, UI (Telegram API), and persistence are intertwined
Scalability limitations due to single-process deployment (monolith)
Testing difficulty as modules cannot be unit-tested in isolation without mocks for shared state (e.g., database session)
